definition: A number $z = a + b\mathrm{i}$, where $a$ and $b$ are real and $\mathrm{i}$ is the non-real number with $\mathrm{i}^{2} = -1$; real numbers are the complex numbers with $b = 0$.
A complex number written as $z = a + b\mathrm{i}$ with $a$ and $b$ real: the real part first, then the imaginary part times $\mathrm{i}$.
For $z = a + b\mathrm{i}$ with $a$ and $b$ real, the real part is $\mathrm{Re}(z) = a$.
For $z = a + b\mathrm{i}$ with $a$ and $b$ real, the imaginary part is the real number $\mathrm{Im}(z) = b$, not $b\mathrm{i}$.

For $z = a + b\mathrm{i}$ with $a$ and $b$ real, the conjugate is $z^{*} = a - b\mathrm{i}$, the reflection of $z$ in the real axis of an Argand diagram; the non-real roots of a quadratic with real coefficients are a conjugate pair.
For $z = a + b\mathrm{i}$ with $a$ and $b$ real, $\lvert z\rvert = \sqrt{a^{2} + b^{2}}$, the distance from $0$ to $z$ on an Argand diagram; it is never negative.

For $z = a + b\mathrm{i} \neq 0$, the angle $\arg z$ from the positive real axis to the line from $0$ to $z$ on an Argand diagram, measured anticlockwise and usually with $-\pi < \arg z \le \pi$; $\arctan\frac{b}{a}$ gives it only when $a > 0$, so check the quadrant.
A drawing of the complex plane, with a horizontal real axis and a vertical imaginary axis, on which $a + b\mathrm{i}$ ($a$, $b$ real) is the point $(a, b)$.

For $ax^{2} + bx + c$ with $a \neq 0$, the number $\Delta = b^{2} - 4ac$; when $a$, $b$ and $c$ are real, $ax^{2} + bx + c = 0$ has two distinct real roots if $\Delta > 0$, one repeated real root if $\Delta = 0$, and no real roots but two complex conjugate roots if $\Delta < 0$.
